date: 2026-09-11
notes: v57 stops the compiler hanging on a half-written .ppu. Give v56 a truncated but non-empty unit file -- what a killed build, a full disk or an interrupted copy leaves behind -- and it spins at 99% CPU forever, prints nothing, and has to be killed. A zero-byte .ppu was already handled correctly and said so, and that is what makes this the compiler's fault and not the file's: the PPU reader treated running off the end of the file as a silent no-op, returning quietly with the destination buffer untouched and telling nobody. The entry header is read through that same path, so at end of file the reader still described the PREVIOUS entry and handed it back to its caller over and over, and the interface loader re-processed it forever. On the reported 120-byte file the cut lands exactly at the end of the source-file-list entry, so what got replayed was the source file list -- a million identical "PPU Source:" lines in twelve seconds. Now a short read sets the reader's error flag, the flag is sticky, the entry reader reports a read error instead of replaying a stale entry, and end-of-entry reports true so the seven draining loops in the unit loader stop. The compiler already had the right fatal for this -- "Invalid PPU-File entry" -- and already stopped on it everywhere; it simply never got told. No new message, no PPU format change, and ppudump already guarded itself with the same flag, so this makes the compiler agree with its own dump tool. MEASURED over 20 truncation offsets of one real 55291-byte .ppu on an identical command line: NINE of the twenty hang on v56, so the reported input was not special, and all nine now exit 1 with a message in 0.05s while the intact file still compiles exit 0. Full 1983-test corpus 1983 SAME 0 DIFF against a baseline rebuilt from the same source minus the patch; self-host fixpoint stage2==stage3 byte-identical. WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64 with the published v56 exe as the control: v56 killed at 25s with no output, v57 fatal + exit 1 in under a second, both exit 0 on the intact unit -- so the harness can still fail. wine is NOT Windows: it runs the real shipped PE bytes through an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API, which is execution evidence for the code we generate and never a real-Windows sign-off. Nobody has yet run any VibePascal release on real Windows hardware. NOT FIXED and not hidden: cutting only the last 11 bytes off that file is still accepted, because nothing an interface load reads lives there; catching it needs a whole-file length check against the header size that also copes with .ppu data read from a nonzero offset inside a stream, which is a riskier change and does not belong in a hang fix. Compiler-binary-only refresh on v56 -- no PPU format, RTL or package change, so UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin alone. Reported by BuildMaster.
